title: Importing XML into Business Central with AL
summary: The post demonstrates how to parse cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language) files in Business Central using AL code without specialized XML codeunits. It walks through a practical example of extracting purchase order data from an XML file and populating custom tables, highlighting the hierarchical node-based navigation required for XML parsing.
key_points: XML files use strict hierarchical structures with nodes and attributes that allow predictable navigation compared to JSON formats
The example uses XmlDocument, XmlNodeList, XmlNode, and XmlElement objects to recursively drill through nested XML elements
cXML is a 1999 standard for commerce data exchange but real-world implementations often deviate from strict schema definitions, requiring manual exception handling
The ParseXML procedure extracts vendor IDs, order headers, line items with quantities, part IDs, descriptions, unit prices, and unit of measure from a sample purchase order

quotes.text: XML files differ from many others in that the XML file should be paired with a definition file.
quotes.why_it_matters: Understanding that XML relies on schema definitions explains why validation against XSD is important for reliable parsing

quotes.text: Because of this strict format we can ask for data within a given node and expect it to be there.
quotes.why_it_matters: Justifies why XML parsing uses static node paths rather than the flexible navigation required for JSON
